content.title: Review idea: regenerate token returns 401 in open auth mode (BUG-1)
content.description: Triage decision needed for idea mqe162cmbi (BUG-1). Phase 4 validation found POST /api/users/:name/regenerate returns 401 in open auth mode — the webapp server route (packages/webapp/server/routes/users.ts:54) calls tracker.usersRegenerate(name) without forwarding the authenticated user context, so resolveAuthor returns 'anonymous' which != target user. See the idea for full root cause. Please decide: ACCEPT (fix as a webapp bug), NEEDS REFINEMENT, or DISCARD. If accept, note the scope/owner so the PM can plan implementation children.

content.content:
TRIAGE DECISION: ACCEPT — fix as a real bug.

Root cause confirmed by code review:
- The webapp regenerate route (packages/webapp/server/routes/users.ts:54) calls tracker.usersRegenerate(name) without forwarding any user token.
- usersRegenerate (packages/library/src/core/tracker.ts:1883) runs resolveAuthor(..., requiresWrite: true), and resolveAuthor (packages/library/src/core/auth.ts:60-75) returns config.auth.defaultUser in open mode ("anonymous" in the validation env).
- usersRegenerate then enforces a self-service check (tracker.ts:1904: callerName !== lowerName). Since caller resolves to the default user, not the target :name, it returns INVALID_TOKEN -> 401.
- This is asymmetric vs register/revoke, which have no self-service check and therefore work fine in open mode.

Scope/owner:
- Primary owner: webapp-developer. The fix must let the webapp authenticate the regenerate on behalf of the named user.
- IMPORTANT nuance for planning: this is NOT a pure webapp-only fix. usersRegenerate has no programmatic auth override — it only reads process.env.AGT_USER_TOKEN or the default user (resolveAuthor supports options.token but usersRegenerate does not expose it). The clean fix is a small, backward-compatible library addition — e.g. usersRegenerate(name, { token }) that forwards into resolveAuthor({ token }) — plus the webapp looking up the target user's token and passing it. Do NOT fix it by setting process.env.AGT_USER_TOKEN around the call (not concurrency-safe — the tracker is a process singleton). So plan it as webapp-developer + library-developer coordination.
- Alternative worth weighing during planning: relax the self-service check in open mode (the webapp is the trusted boundary in open mode, and register/revoke already trust the caller there). This is library-only but changes security semantics — flag for review.

Acceptance:
- e2e/packages/webapp/e2e/phase4-validation.spec.ts:197-216 currently asserts the 401 and must be flipped to assert success (201 + new token). That test currently locks the bug in as passing, so updating it is part of the fix, not optional.
- Backend 'Can regenerate a token' (Phase 4) should then be fully met, not partial.

Handing back to PM to plan implementation children.
